summary: A native select with label, description and error built in, taking part in forms. Options are plain <option> and <optgroup> children.

label.note: Visible label and accessible name. Required: shadow DOM keeps external <label for> from reaching the inner select.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name.

errorMessage.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid.

value.note: Value of the selected option; submitted with the form. Without it, the option marked selected (else the first option) is the default restored by form reset.

required.note: Native required: the selected option must have a non-empty value. Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Vertical stack with the field gap.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Positions the chevron over the select.

anatomy.name: select
anatomy.notes: Native <select>, appearance none; its <option> and <optgroup> children mirror the host's light-DOM ones.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each selection change. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Selection committed. Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed (NativeControl).

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring and border in ring color (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

error.trigger: error-message set, or native validity fails after blur or a submit attempt

accessibility.role: combobox (a native single-selection <select>; listbox when size > 1)
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: ElementInternals: setFormValue(value), validity mirrored from the inner select (required -> valueMissing) with setValidity, formResetCallback restores the default selection, disabled is not submitted.

accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the select; 3px ring in native-select.focus-ring.color.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.ArrowUp / ArrowDown: change or move through options (platform behavior)
keyboard.typing: jump to the option starting with the typed text

aria: aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required on the select; the asterisk is aria-hidden
errorMessage: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
announcements: error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: Choose one value from a known list, especially on mobile or in a long form
A value must be picked before submit
useCases.use: required with a first <option value=""> prompt

antiPatterns.pattern: Few options (2 to 4) where all should be visible
antiPatterns.why: A closed select hides the choices

antiPatterns.pattern: A prompt option with a real value
antiPatterns.why: It is submitted as a valid choice
antiPatterns.alternative: A first prompt option with an empty value ("Select…") plus required

coverage: label is the name; label click focuses; 36px and small 32px
light-DOM options, optgroups and disabled mirrored, and updated when children change
selection updates value; input and change composed once
hide-label keeps the name; chevron aria-hidden, no pointer events
description and error in the accessible description; aria-invalid
required: native required, aria-hidden asterisk, invalid after blur
form value, selected default, validity, reset, disabled, disabled fieldset, errorMessage customError, label for

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: the native select keeps its platform keyboard model; label above like Input.

openQuestions.question: Separate sb-native-select-option and sb-native-select-optgroup elements, or plain light-DOM children?
openQuestions.answer: Plain light-DOM <option> and <optgroup> children, mirrored into the shadow <select> by a MutationObserver. Simplest and most robust: no extra elements or contexts, authors keep native markup, and a native <option> never needs to render itself. The children are not slotted (they stay unrendered);

openQuestions.question: Which option is selected by default?
openQuestions.answer: The value attribute if set, else the option with the selected attribute, else the first option, like a native select. Form reset restores it.
